Actual use is nine files and sixty distinct glyphs: components/scanner/tech-icon.tsx:1-60 imports one `IconType`, `GrHeroku`, `FaMagento` and fifty-five `Si*` brand icons for the software-inventory panel, and the remaining eight files (components/auth/oauth-buttons.tsx:3-4, components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:47-48, components/profile/tabs/profile-social-tab.tsx:6-7, components/profile/tabs/profile-billing-tab.tsx:27, components/scanner/footer.tsx:5, components/modals/github-profile-modal.tsx:9, components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx:2, app/docs/developers/page.tsx:8) between them use exactly three: `FaGithub`, `FaDiscord`, `FcGoogle`. This is an install-size and cold-build cost, not a bundle-size one: the per-icon module layout tree-shakes cleanly, so AUDIT-012#fe-01 and #fe-02's client-bundle findings are not what this is about. The cost lands on the CI npm cache, the Docker builder layer and `npm ci` wall time on every one of the five CI jobs.
impact: 85 MB of the 789 MB node_modules, restored and re-cached on every CI job and every image build, for sixty SVG paths. It also inflates the `npm ci` step that runs five times per push across the lint, typecheck, test, extension and build jobs.
recommendation: This one is worth doing only if the CI or image time actually matters, since it is a mechanical but broad change. The lighter path for the fifty-five brand glyphs in components/scanner/tech-icon.tsx is `@icons-pack/react-simple-icons`, which wraps the same Simple Icons set at a fraction of the install size, or inlining the sixty SVG path strings into a local map in that file (they are static paths, a few KB total). The three OAuth glyphs used across the other eight files are the same three every time and are the obvious first candidates to inline, which alone removes react-icons from eight of the nine importers.

title: eslint-config-next is on major 16 while next is on major 15, so the lint rule set targets a framework major the app is not running
description: package.json:95 pins `next: 15.5.23`; package.json:131 pins `eslint-config-next: 16.3.2`, which in turn hard-depends on `@next/eslint-plugin-next: 16.3.2` (per the lockfile entry for eslint-config-next). The jump was deliberate and is explained at eslint.config.mjs:3-6: eslint-config-next 16 is the first release with native flat config, so moving to it let the repo drop the `@eslint/eslintrc` FlatCompat shim, and eslint.config.mjs:13 imports `eslint-config-next/core-web-vitals` directly. The side effect is that the Next-specific rules being enforced are the Next 16 set: rules added or changed for Next 16 conventions run against a Next 15 codebase, and rules removed in 16 for patterns Next 15 still has are not enforced at all. This also puts the two out of dependabot's `next-stack` group's reach as a unit, since .github/dependabot.yml:75-77 ignores `next` majors while `eslint-config-next` has already taken one.
impact: Bounded and mostly latent: the lint job either flags a Next 16 idiom the app cannot adopt yet, or stops flagging a Next 15 anti-pattern because the rule was dropped in 16. Neither breaks the build, but it means the `lint` gate's Next coverage is not the coverage the running framework needs, and there is no signal anywhere that says so.
recommendation: Add a comment at package.json:131 (or in eslint.config.mjs beside the import at line 13) recording that eslint-config-next is intentionally one major ahead of next and why, so the next person to read the manifest does not treat it as a mistake or 'fix' it downward. Revisit when the Next 16 upgrade lands and the two realign.

title: The four manifests disagree about Node: cli declares >=18 (EOL since April 2025) while root and extension declare >=22, marketing declares nothing, and CI only ever runs the CLI on Node 22
description: `cli/package.json:16` declares `"node": ">=18"`, `package.json:8` declares `"node": ">=22.0.0"`, `extension/package.json:9` declares `"node": ">=22.0.0"`, and `marketing/package.json` declares no `engines` field at all. The Node 18 claim is repeated to users in three places: `cli/README.md:5` ("no dependencies (Node 18+ for global fetch)"), `cli/vulnradar.mjs:4` ("No dependencies: Node 18+ (global fetch) is all it needs"), and the docs page at `app/docs/cli/page.tsx:95` ("It needs Node 18 or newer"). Node 18 reached end of life on 2025-04-30 and receives no security updates. It is also never exercised: the only place the CLI runs in CI is `.github/workflows/ci.yml:110`, `node --test` with `working-directory: cli`, inside the `test` job whose `setup-node` step pins `node-version: "22"` (line 47). So the supported-floor claim is asserted in three user-facing places and validated in none. Node's own `--test` runner also behaved differently in 18 (experimental, narrower default file-glob) than in 22, so `node --test` with no path argument is not guaranteed to discover `cli/vulnradar.test.mjs` there.
impact: A user or a CI pipeline pinned to Node 18 follows the documented floor, runs the CLI on a runtime that has had no security patches for over a year, and hits any regression alone because nothing tests that version. Meanwhile a contributor who reads the root manifest reasonably assumes Node 22 is the repo-wide floor and may use a Node 20-or-22-only API in cli/lib.mjs without any check catching it.
recommendation: Raise `cli/package.json:16` to `">=20"` (the oldest Node still in maintenance) or to `">=22"` to match the other three manifests, and update the three copy sites: `cli/README.md:5`, the header comment at `cli/vulnradar.mjs:4`, and `app/docs/cli/page.tsx:95`. If Node 18 support is genuinely wanted, add a matrix entry to the CLI test step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml:110` that runs `node --test` on 18 as well. Also add `"engines": { "node": ">=22.0.0" }` to `marketing/package.json` so all four agree.

title: cli/package.json is publishable but incomplete: no `private` flag, a `name` that collides with the root manifest, no `repository`, and a `files` list that omits the license it declares
description: `cli/package.json` declares `"name": "vulnradar"` (line 2), `"license": "GPL-3.0"` (line 5), a `bin` entry (line 7), and `"files": ["vulnradar.mjs", "lib.mjs", "README.md"]` (line 10). It has no `"private": true`, so `npm publish` from that directory would succeed. Three things are missing or wrong for that path. The `name` is identical to the root manifest's `"name": "vulnradar"` at `package.json:2`, which is only harmless because the root sets `"private": true` at line 6; the CLI does not. There is no `repository` field, so the published page would carry no source link and no npm provenance attestation. And `files` omits any license file (there is none in `cli/` to include), so a GPL-3.0 tarball would ship without its license text. On the positive side the package is genuinely dependency-free: `cli/vulnradar.mjs` imports only `./lib.mjs`, `cli/lib.mjs` imports nothing, and both use only global `fetch`, `process` and `console`, so there is no accidental dependency on the app's runtime and no lockfile is needed. This finding is the mechanical half of subdeps-01: fixing that one means publishing this manifest, and it is not ready.
impact: A publish today produces a package with no repo link, no provenance, and no license file, under a name that shadows the root manifest. Minor on its own, but subdeps-01 argues the name should be claimed soon, and this is what has to be corrected first.
recommendation: Before publishing, add `"repository": { "type": "git", "url": "git+https://github.com/VulnRadar/vulnradar.dev.git", "directory": "cli" }` to `cli/package.json`, add a `LICENSE` file in `cli/` and list it in `files` at line 10, and publish with `npm publish --provenance` from CI so the tarball carries a signed attestation.

title: vitest collects only .test.ts, so a .test.tsx file is silently never run, and with no DOM environment or testing-library dependency no component can be rendered in a test at all
description: vitest.config.ts:24 sets `include: ["tests/**/*.test.ts", "tests/**/*.spec.ts"]` and line 23 sets `environment: "node"`. Neither `.test.tsx` nor `.spec.tsx` is collected, and package.json declares no jsdom, happy-dom, @testing-library/react, or @testing-library/dom dependency (grep returns nothing for all four). Counted: tests/ holds 356 `.test.ts` files, 0 `.spec.ts`, and 0 `.test.tsx`. The 8 files under tests/components/ test only extracted pure helpers (queue-status-utils, settings-registry-utils, utils, danger-score-trend), not components. The mechanical failure: a contributor adds `tests/components/scanner/scan-form.test.tsx`, runs `npm test`, gets a normal green run with no warning that their file was not collected (vitest reports nothing about files outside `include`), and ships. Even a `.test.ts` file that imported a component would fail, since `environment: "node"` supplies no document.
impact: Two effects. First, a contributor can believe they have shipped a test that has never run once, which is worse than no test. Second, none of the 266 .tsx files under components/ has any behavioural test, so hook state, conditional rendering, and event handlers are covered only by the typechecker. Given the AUDIT-011 critical finding was a UI regression (admin row actions invisible but still hit-testable on touch), that gap is the one most likely to recur.
recommendation: Add `"tests/**/*.test.tsx"` and `"tests/**/*.spec.tsx"` to `include` in vitest.config.ts:24 so a .tsx suite cannot be silently skipped. If component tests are wanted, add jsdom plus @testing-library/react as devDependencies and set `environment` per file via the `// @vitest-environment jsdom` docblock rather than switching the whole suite off node.

title: jspdf and jspdf-autotable are production dependencies with zero imports, and vitest plus @vitest/coverage-v8 are in dependencies rather than devDependencies
description: package.json:92-93 declares jspdf 4.2.1 and jspdf-autotable 5.0.8 as runtime dependencies. A repo-wide grep for jspdf/jsPDF across every .ts, .tsx and .mjs outside node_modules, .next and the stale worktree returns exactly one hit, and it is a comment: tests/lib/reports/pdf-report.test.ts:8 ('browser-rendering dependency here despite jspdf being in package.json for'). Nothing imports either package. Separately, @vitest/coverage-v8 4.1.11 (package.json:81) and vitest 4.1.11 (package.json:117) are listed under `dependencies` rather than devDependencies, so `npm ci --omit=dev` in a Docker build installs the whole test runner and its v8 coverage toolchain into the production image.
impact: Three unnecessary packages are installed, audited and shipped in every production install and Docker image. The two jspdf packages are also a live supply-chain surface for code that does not exist, and their presence implies a PDF export path that a reader of package.json would go looking for.
recommendation: Remove jspdf and jspdf-autotable from package.json dependencies (and update the comment at tests/lib/reports/pdf-report.test.ts:8), and move vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 from dependencies to devDependencies. Regenerate package-lock.json on Linux or graft the entries, per the lockfile-platform constraint this repo already documents.

title: The server config module lands in the root-layout client chunk, carrying dead process.env.SMTP_PASS and BROWSERBASE_API_KEY reads into every page's JavaScript
description: lib/config/constants.ts (787 lines) re-exports lib/config/config-values.ts (1,367 lines) and is imported directly by client components across the app, including ones mounted in app/layout.tsx. The compiled result is visible in the committed build: static/chunks/9711-3989d97c24edd68e.js, 18 KB and part of the /layout entry (so present on all 311 routes), contains `i.env.SMTP_HOST, i.env.SMTP_PORT, i.env.SMTP_USER, i.env.SMTP_PASS, i.env.SMTP_FROM||i.env.SMTP_USER;` and `i.env.BROWSERBASE_API_KEY&&i.env.BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID;` as bare expression statements alongside the team-role matrix and the API route table. No secret is disclosed: `i` is Next's client process shim and only NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed variables are inlined, so these evaluate to undefined -- but the code and the variable names ship, and every unused constant webpack cannot prove dead ships with them.
impact: Every page in the app carries a slice of the server configuration module and dead environment reads for SMTP credentials and the Browserbase API key. It is bytes and noise today, and it is one careless `NEXT_PUBLIC_` rename away from becoming a real disclosure, since the read sites are already compiled into a client chunk.
recommendation: Enforce the split the project already documents in CLAUDE.md: keep lib/config/client-constants.ts as the only module client components import, move the process.env-reading blocks (EMAIL_CONFIG and the Browserbase configured check in lib/config/constants.ts) into a server-only module marked with `import "server-only"`, and change the client-side imports of @/lib/config/constants over to the client-safe module.

title: Dead configuration objects and constants, including a FEATURES object where seven of eight members are unread
description: The FEATURES object at lib/config/constants.ts:778-786 has exactly one live member: a grep for FEATURES.[A-Z_]+ outside lib/config returns one hit, lib/hooks/use-client-config.ts:33 reading .PDF_REPORTS. The other seven (DEMO_MODE, TEAMS, API_KEYS, WEBHOOKS, SCHEDULED_SCANS, BULK_SCANS, EMAIL_NOTIFICATIONS) are read nowhere; the underlying CONFIG_FEATURE_* values are alive via the registry, so only this convenience object is dead. Also dead: the DATABASE object (:478-484, no matches for DATABASE.[A-Z_]), PATTERNS (:338), PAGINATION (:500), ENTERPRISE_EMAIL (:641), AUTH_SESSION_MAX_AGE (:242), API_KEY_SCOPE_DESCRIPTIONS (client-constants.ts:346), CONFIG_API_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS (config-values.ts:660), CONFIG_FOOTER_TEXT (:191), HISTORY_REPORT (client-constants.ts:151, zero web callers - the export menu regenerates all five formats client-side, and only the extension uses the route). Catalog helpers getFreePlan (catalog.ts:305), isPaidPlan (:309) and getApiLimitForPlan (:318) have tests as their only callers. Five unused skeleton exports at components/admin/shared/skeleton.tsx:18,40,62,90,114 (about 110 lines). components/auth/auth-layout.tsx:9-11 documents a width="wide" prop no caller uses - see auth-11, which is the screen it was written for. lib/config/public-paths.ts:66 lists ROUTES.GDPR_REQUEST as "/legal/privacy#gdpr" but middleware.ts:265 matches on pathname, which never contains a fragment, so the entry can never match (harmless, line 49 covers it).
impact: Cleanup only, but the HISTORY_REPORT case has a real consequence: the server route additionally runs attachRemediation (app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:149-155), so extension-exported reports and web-exported reports are not byte-identical.
recommendation: Deletions need owner sign-off. The one to act on regardless is the report divergence: decide whether the extension and the web app should produce the same file, and make them agree.

title: Two parsed environment variables are never consulted, one of them documented
description: CONTACT_EMAIL is parsed at lib/config/env.ts:85 and appears in .env.example and the docs, but the contact route sends to NOREPLY_EMAIL (app/api/v3/contact/route.ts:146). STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is parsed at :60 while only the NEXT_PUBLIC_ variant is ever read.
impact: A self-hoster sets CONTACT_EMAIL as documented and contact mail goes elsewhere.
recommendation: Either honour CONTACT_EMAIL in the contact route or remove it from env.ts, .env.example and the docs. Remove the unused STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY parse.

title: The opt-in screenshot wait is capped at 30 seconds, longer than the entire rest of the scan
description: lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:812 awaits the screenshot with CONFIG_SCAN_SCREENSHOT_MAX_WAIT_MS = 30_000 (lib/config/config-values.ts:1013).
impact: Only affects users who tick the box, but when it bites it more than doubles the wait.
recommendation: Reduce the cap, or render results first and let the screenshot populate asynchronously.

title: CSP connect-src has trailing https: wss: wildcards
description: CSP connect-src 'self' https://challenges.cloudflare.com ... https://www.browserbase.com wss://*.browserbase.com https: wss: ends with the scheme-only wildcards https: wss:, which permits fetch/XHR/WS to any HTTPS origin.
recommendation: Drop the trailing 'https:' 'wss:' scheme wildcards; allowlist specific API hosts.

title: docker-publish.yml dual-tags :latest in GHCR
description: Every tagged release also pushes :latest. Anyone running :latest (despite compose using :3.0.0) gets an unreviewed mutable reference.
recommendation: Drop the second -t $IMAGE:latest + matching docker push $IMAGE:latest.

title: docker-compose app port binds to 0.0.0.0
description: Short-form binding defaults to 0.0.0.0:3000. Self-hosters fronted by nginx expose Node directly on the LAN.

title: package.json engines allows Node 20 (EOL)
description: engines allows Node 20 which reached EOL on 2026-04-30 per the Dockerfile comment. Yet package.json still accepts Node 20 dev environments.
recommendation: Drop the '<21.0.0' branch from engines.node.

title: Sixteen packages are behind, and only next and typescript are majors: both are deliberately held, and the rest are minor or patch drift with no security content
description: `npm outdated --json` lists sixteen entries. Two are majors and both are held on purpose, documented in .github/dependabot.yml:73-81. (a) `next` 15.5.23 vs 16.3.3 (package.json:95), with `update-types: ["version-update:semver-major"]` ignored so the Next 16 jump arrives as a manual decision rather than an automated PR. Next 15.5.23 is well past the 15.2.3 that fixed the middleware-bypass advisory and npm audit reports nothing against it, so this is a planning item, not a security one, though see deps-13 for the eslint-config-next half of it having already moved. (b) `typescript` 6.0.3 vs 7.0.2 (package.json:135), held because `@typescript-eslint/*` 8.67.0 declares `typescript: ">=4.8.4 <6.1.0"`, so TS 7 would break both the lint and typecheck CI jobs; dependabot.yml:78-81 states exactly this. The other fourteen are minors and patches with no advisory content: @ai-sdk/anthropic and @ai-sdk/openai and `ai` (all unused, see deps-01), @types/node 26.2.0 vs 26.4.0, @types/react-dom, @typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin and parser 8.67.0 vs 8.68.0, eslint-config-next 16.3.2 vs 16.3.3, lucide-react 1.34.0 vs 1.35.0, nodemailer 9.0.5 vs 9.0.6, stripe 22.5.0 vs 22.6.0, and zod 4.4.3 vs 4.5.2. Note that `npm outdated`'s `current` column here reflects a workspace whose node_modules has drifted below the lockfile in three places (eslint 10.8.1 installed against 10.9.0 locked, @ai-sdk/anthropic 4.0.40 against a `^4.0.41` floor, react-hook-form 7.85.0 against an exact 7.86.0 pin), which is a local-install artifact, not a repo state: `npm ci` on CI resolves the locked versions and the CI run on main is green.
impact: None urgent. The one thing worth tracking is the typescript hold: it is correctly reasoned and correctly documented today, but it couples the TypeScript version the whole codebase compiles against to a single lint plugin's peer range, so it needs revisiting when typescript-eslint ships TS 7 support rather than being left to drift.
recommendation: No action needed on the fourteen minors beyond letting dependabot's weekly PRs land. Add a dated note to the typescript ignore rule at .github/dependabot.yml:78-81 so the hold is revisited rather than becoming permanent, and treat the Next 16 upgrade as its own scheduled piece of work given deps-13 shows the lint half already moved ahead of it.

title: Negative result for the next audit: the four config surfaces share no duplicated export, all 271 registry defaults derive from CONFIG_ constants, and all seven paginated routes use the same page/limit convention
description:
I checked the specific split-brain shape AUDIT-009#dup-01 found (RATE_LIMITS defined in two places so 11 routes bypassed the admin-configured values) against the current tree and it has not recurred.

Extracting every `export const` and `export function` from lib/config/constants.ts (788 lines), lib/config/client-constants.ts (378), lib/config/config-values.ts (1,368), lib/config/registry.ts, lib/config/brand.ts and lib/config/env.ts gives zero names exported from more than one of them. The layering holds in the direction it is documented: config-values.ts holds the literals, constants.ts imports and re-exports them (RATE_LIMITS at constants.ts:360-470 is built entirely from CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_* imports, with no second literal anywhere), and client-constants.ts is re-exported through constants.ts rather than redefined.

lib/config/registry.ts contains 272 `default:` entries and every one of them is a CONFIG_ constant imported from config-values.ts, not a literal, so an admin-editable setting cannot fall back to a value that disagrees with the compiled one. The comment at registry.ts:1-11 describes that rule and the code follows it.

Separately, every paginated endpoint uses the same query convention: `page` and `limit` in all seven (app/api/v3/admin/route.ts, admin/content, admin/email-logs, admin/error-logs, admin/teams, ai/conversations, public-scans). Nothing uses offset or a cursor. The response-side key drift is filed as dup-08; the request side is consistent.

The brand palette is likewise consolidated: lib/config/brand.ts is the single source and lib/email/email.ts:19-47 aliases it rather than holding its own hexes, which is what the comment at brand.ts:1-13 claims.
impact: None. Recorded so the next audit does not spend time re-deriving these four surfaces or re-checking pagination conventions.
recommendation: No action. Keep the registry.ts:1-11 rule ("Adding a configurable value means adding an entry here, not a bare constant") enforced in review; it is the thing preventing the AUDIT-009 shape from returning.

title: Several compiled config constants orphaned after their routes migrated to admin-configurable settings this session
description: AUTH_SESSION_MAX_AGE, DEVICE_TRUST_MAX_AGE, DEFAULT_API_KEY_DAILY_LIMIT, and the PAGINATION constant object all have zero remaining importers after their call sites correctly migrated to getSetting()-based values this session. Not wrong today, but a future caller grepping for these could grab the frozen constant instead of the live setting with no compiler error to catch it.
recommendation: Delete the orphaned constants now that nothing consumes them, or mark them clearly as legacy-default-only.

title: AUTH_SECRET not set in .env.local
description: AUTH_SECRET is optional. On the deployed sandbox the fallback to API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY is in use. If that key is ever rotated, OAuth state tokens issued under the previous HMAC key silently fail to verify.
recommendation: Generate and set AUTH_SECRET in .env.local; document it as a separate 32+ char secret.
